conventions.convention: Cellular chains and incidence multiplicities use F₂. Loops, multiple edges and repeated face-edge incidences are allowed; both primal and dual graphs must be connected. No cell orientation is required.
The canonical Pauli is P(a,b)=X(a)Z(b), without an arbitrary scalar phase; vertex stabilizers are X(∂₁ᵀv), and face stabilizers are Z(∂₂f).
The Hamiltonian uses positive penalties J_v(I−A_v)/2 and K_f(I−B_f)/2. Thus one violated vertex or face constraint costs J_v or K_f respectively.

Square-torus results require L≥3. Complementary primal and dual coordinate cycles satisfy I(p_i,q_j)=δ_ij; local compression requires a supporting disk whose complement contains all four representatives.
The spectral gap is the least positive Hamiltonian eigenvalue, with value +∞ when no positive eigenvalue exists. The genus-dependent theorem explicitly assumes the Axiom of Choice.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite closed-surface cellulation, H_K=Σ_v J_v(I−A_v)/2+Σ_f K_f(I−B_f)/2, with positive coefficients, A_v=X(∂₁ᵀv), B_f=Z(∂₂f), and ∂₁∂₂=0.

On the square L×L torus, L≥3, if P(a,b) has the stated disk support and complementary cycles and commutes with every stabilizer, then a=∂₁ᵀu and b=∂₂w for vertex and face chains u,w. Consequently P(a,b) is a product of stabilizers.

Assuming the Axiom of Choice, a finite cellulation of a closed connected orientable genus-g surface has a positive, frustration-free toric Hamiltonian with ground-space dimension 2^(2g) and gap at least 2m. On the uniform square L×L torus, L≥3, the exact gap is 2 min(J,K).

Assuming the Axiom of Choice on the square L×L torus, L≥3, closed primal Z and dual X strings have commutation sign (−1)^I. Every operator supported in the stated disk with complementary coordinate cycles satisfies P₀OP₀=λ(O)P₀.
